Starting point

Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern, C3 D3 E3 F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, through the test MIDI device at 90 BPM with Rate /1 and channel range steps 1-4. The sequencer is stopped and a MIDI keyboard is connected as Mosaic's input. Every Mosaic option is at its default, so Map scale to white keys and the three Honour switches are Off, and the Scale Editor is on C major.

Notice the screen and grid result of the action above.

Current action MIDI (starting view; earlier output not shown here): none.

NEXT ACTION

Play some keys on the keyboard: each sounds the note you pressed, because nothing is mapped yet. Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC > Midi control. Select Map scale to white keys and turn E3 right to On. The row reads On.

captures.final_text_excerpt:
the Honour switches control whether the Scale Editor’s degree, rotation and transpose settings affect that mapping.

Baseline: in PARAMS > MOSAIC > Midi control, set Map scale to white keys On. In the Scale Editor select C natural minor, set degree II, rotation 2 and global transpose +2. Set Honour scale degree On, Honour scale rotations Off and Honour scale transpose Off. Play MIDI keys 60 through 72 chromatically at velocity 90. Output: 62, 63, 63, 65, 65, 67, 68, 68, 70, 70, 72, 72, 74.
Rotation comparison: turn Honour scale rotations On and replay MIDI keys 60 through 72 at velocity 90. Output: 62, 63, 63, 65, 65, 67, 68, 68, 58, 58, 60, 60, 74. The last two scale positions are an octave lower.
RECIPE 02
Apply scale rotation and global transpose to every keyboard key

Goal: compare the same incoming MIDI keys with Honour scale transpose Off and On. Map scale to white keys lays the selected scale on white keys; each Honour switch controls whether its named Scale Editor transformation participates.

Baseline: in PARAMS > MOSAIC > Midi control, set Map scale to white keys On. In the Scale Editor select C natural minor, set degree II, rotation 2 and global transpose +2. Set Honour scale degree and Honour scale rotations On, and Honour scale transpose Off. Play MIDI keys 60 through 72 chromatically at velocity 90. Output: 62, 63, 63, 65, 65, 67, 68, 68, 58, 58, 60, 60, 74.
Transpose comparison: turn Honour scale transpose On and replay the same keys at velocity 90. Output: 64, 65, 65, 67, 67, 69, 70, 70, 60, 60, 62, 62, 76. Every mapped note is two semitones higher.

Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern, C3 D3 E3 F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, through the test MIDI device at 90 BPM with Rate /1 and channel range steps 1-4. The sequencer is stopped and a MIDI keyboard is connected as Mosaic's input. Map scale to white keys is On and the scale is C natural minor. The Scale Editor holds degree II, rotation 2 and global transpose +2, and Honour scale degree is On, so the white keys C3 to C4 play 62, 63, 65, 67, 68, 70, 72, 74. Honour scale rotations and Honour scale transpose are Off.

Notice the screen and grid result of the action above.

Current action MIDI (starting view; earlier output not shown here): none.

NEXT ACTION

Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC > Midi control. Select Honour scale rotations and turn E3 right to On. The row reads On.

steps.label:
02
After
Turn on Honour scale rotations
steps.excerpt:
02
After
Turn on Honour scale rotations

Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC > Midi control. Select Honour scale rotations and turn E3 right to On. The row reads On.

Notice the screen and grid result of the action above.

Recorded MIDI output: none.

NEXT ACTION

Close the menu and play C3 to C4 again. Rotation 2 turns the top of the scale upside down: the last two white keys before the octave, the A and B keys, sound an octave lower, 58 and 60 instead of 70 and 72, giving 62, 63, 65, 67, 68, 58, 60, 74. The first five keys do not change. Use it to play a bass note or an inverted voicing of the same scale shape from the keys you already know.
